Sigma Beam System Designer EN 1993-1-3 · main beam + secondary Type A / Type B

Floor element (panel, grating, MDF) → secondary beams → main beam → column → base → floor slab. Type A secondaries frame into the main beam; Type B secondaries frame into the columns. Restraints, panels and connections are credited only when their stiffness and strength are demonstrated. Same calculations as the Excel workbook (revision 8): bays and modules with the load chain, direct welds at the top and bottom of built-up pairs, bolt groups nv × nh placed from the first bolt below the top of the section, the omega L-cleat through the main-web holes, restraints credited only when demonstrated (with their basis), live finite-strip kdist, failure cards with the reason, remedy and a link to the governing input, and a printable complete design report.

Inputs-
Main beam-
Type A-

Max utilisation-
Governing-

Units: dimensions mm; area loads kg/m² (converted to kN/m²); forces kN; moments kN·m; stresses N/mm²; stiffness kN/mm (lateral) and kN·cm/rad (rotational; panel Cθ in kN·cm/cm/rad). Automatic values (C1, k_dist, L_LT, restraint spacings, support fixity, tributary widths, tab height and spacing, the Sigma middle band) are calculated and are not inputs; they are listed on the design tabs.

Hand-method implementation of EN 1993-1-3 with EN 1993-1-1 (incl. Annex BB.2), EN 1993-1-5, EN 1993-1-8 and EN 1990; nodal-brace requirements from AISC 360-16 Appendix 6. Loads are example values. Results are for checking and must be verified by a qualified engineer.
